nm: poseswap plan, as a railroad diagram

s.t: Next, inside the relay, then the AUX route: from an image or a mesh to labelled, rigged garment parts.
Every box also needs its own repository to pass its gate (not drawn). Most of this slice has not been timed; only the loads, the edit and the score have.
The relay is transport-zone-relay: a C state machine equal to the router model, on two UDP sockets and a 64 Hz tick.
Each box waits for the rails into it. Two ways to route (the model or the relay) and two ways to agree (replicas or pass through) are both drawn.
Part 1. From a moving body to an edited, scored image
Checked against the router model's recorded trace (210 ticks). The sockets are checked on loopback on one machine only; no real network.
A viewer gets six frames a send interval: two from each of the three others. A frame that comes too soon is refused and counted, and its bytes are not copied.
A taken frame is copied in and handed out unchanged, and sent on as it arrives, so none waits in the relay longer than one tick.
or a half taken too soon
transport-zone-relay, in C. Strict C99, no heap, and it never reads a byte of a frame. A zone is four people; a frame is 1,200 bytes.
Inside the relay: one loop, 64 times a second
The total leaves out the image-to-mesh steps and the presence slice: none of them has been timed.
Longest chain, in red: build cloth simulator > measure part lag > soft or rigid > rig the parts. It sets the 91 minutes.
The planner's route for the AUX goal. A step starts when everything feeding it has finished. Dashed is the other way to get a mesh.
